entries.prompt: A production-ready low-resolution side-view pixel-art motion sheet for an adult fantasy action-game character. Use the uploaded canonical motion sheet as the identity and pixel-density reference. Keep the same face, hair, fully worn clothes/armour, equipment, limited palette and crisp outline. Improve pose clarity and clean pixel clusters rather than adding finer-resolution painted detail. Fixed camera and consistent body scale across cells, one complete pose per cell, generous transparent margins, no text, labels, grid lines, enemies or scene background. The character is Adela; body height in the final normalized game art is 62 pixels. Sheet layout 4 columns by 2 rows. Row 1, four successive frames: stunned upright with arms pulled back, losing balance while restrained from behind, collapsing to knees, falling onto side. Row 2, four successive frames: braced against a heavy overhead impact, impact and knees buckling, thrown down, motionless on ground. Make transitions readable. Fully clothed throughout. Do not depict the attacker.

entries.prompt: Edit this existing gothic pixel-art HP HUD sheet, retaining its established materials and the identities of its three components. Make exactly three separate complete components in one horizontal row with wide empty transparent gaps, same front view and matching circle centres/scales. LEFT: the empty grey/silver clear-glass HP orb, with gentle grey internal glass shading and crisp small highlights, no liquid. REMOVE its ornate gold exterior frame completely; give the glass only a very thin neutral dark-grey outline so it can sit inside either separate ornament without two gold frames colliding. MIDDLE: the saint's separate ornate dark-gold halo ring with the original delicate chains; its central circular opening stays entirely transparent and contains no glass orb. RIGHT: the knight's separate ring ornament with a straight longsword and a small kite-shield motif around the outside; its central circular opening stays entirely transparent and contains no glass orb. Keep the opening diameter and location identical in the two ornaments so one shared glass orb fits either. Preserve the gothic dark-gold and iron palette and crisp low-resolution pixel-art style; clean up clusters and small details rather than adding finely painted texture. One component per regular cell, do not join them together, do not bake a glass orb into either ornament, no extra icons, text, labels, visible grid, backdrop, drop-shadow ground or scenery. Output only these three assets on a genuinely transparent background.
entries.previous_unexecuted_spritecook_prompt: Three separate matching low-resolution gothic pixel-art UI components in a single horizontal row, generous transparent spacing, no text or characters. Right: a separate knight ornament with sword and shield, sized to surround the same orb. Keep the orb rim visually light so it does not collide with the two optional outer ornaments when layered. Consistent palette and pixel size. Transparent centres in the ornaments. Do not bake an orb into the ornament components.

entries.prompt: Image 1 is the EXISTING SHEET TO EDIT; image 2 is the EXACT APPROVED in-game character design. Preserve the actual face, hairstyle and hair length, outfit/armour shapes, proportions, equipment and palette shown in image 2. Do not reinterpret or redesign the character. Improve deliberate crisp low-resolution pixel clusters and pose clarity while preserving the original small character scale. Exactly nine complete sprites in a regular three-column by three-row layout, generous transparent gaps, no overlap or cropped equipment. This is Cecilia: keep her very long pale silver hair and trailing pale strands, small profile face, original ornate fitted bodice and shoulder/arm details, long layered pale/lavender skirt panels, original footwear and small chain weapon. Do not shorten the hair or change her into a plain cream robe with a broad dark waistband. The dress stays the same length and design as it moves; show the walking rhythm in the feet and flowing lower panels without replacing the outfit. Reading order: cells 1,2,3 are three distinct reactions to a floor spike below the feet: sharp flinch, recoiling with back arched, recovering balance. Do not put slime under these three. Cells 4,5,6,7 are FOUR CLEARLY DIFFERENT slow-walking poses through ankle-deep olive-green slime: right-foot forward contact with the other foot behind, passing pose with the rear foot lifted and moving forward, left-foot forward contact with the other foot behind, opposite passing pose with that foot lifted. Alternate the leading leg and the arm swing, change the feet and lower-body/skirt folds visibly. Do not repeat four nearly identical standing or bracing silhouettes. Keep the torso's identity and outfit design stable. Facing right in ALL nine frames, never mirror the character to fake the walk. Only feet and ankles touch the green slime, with small sticky drips trailing the moving foot. Cells 8,9 are two subtle idle breathing poses in ankle-deep slime. Fully clothed throughout. No enemy, extra person, text, labels, grid lines, floor scenery or coloured backdrop. Output the sheet only, with actual transparent alpha.
